records.source: Καταβάντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί.
records.gloss: Having come down then of him from the mountain followed him crowds great.
pieces: Great crowds followed Jesus as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came down from the mountain.

L.1: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come down from the mountain, great crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.1: Jesus came down from the hill, and large crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: came down from the mountain: the end of the sermon begun at 5:1
decisions.reason: Matthew links the deeds of chapters 8-9 to the words of chapters 5-7. The same crowds who heard the sermon (7:28) now see what Jesus does.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Jesus heals a man with leprosy

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ λεπρὸς προσελθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
records.gloss: And behold, a leper having come was bowing to him saying, Lord, if you are willing you are able me to cleanse.
pieces: Just then a man with leprosy came up and bowed down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Lord," he said, "if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make me clean."

L.2: And look, a leper came and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make me clean."

R.2: A man who had a bad skin disease came to Jesus and bowed down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can heal me and make me clean."

decisions.choice: leper: a person with a skin disease that made him unclean
alternatives: a person with Hansen's disease only
decisions.reason: The law's word covered a range of skin diseases (Leviticus 13). A person declared unclean had to live apart and warn others away (Leviticus 13:45-46).

decisions.choice: make me clean: heal me, so that I am clean before the law
decisions.reason: Being healed would let him return to worship and to his community.

decisions.choice: knelt before him: bowed low in honor and appeal
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 2:2 and 4:9. Here it is the bow of one asking a great favor.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address, and in Matthew more than that
decisions.reason: The word was a polite address to a superior. In Matthew those who come in faith call Jesus "Lord" (8:2, 6, 8, 25), and the reader hears the full sense.

decisions.choice: look (L); just then (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: a man with leprosy (B); a man who had a bad skin disease (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the person rather than labeling him.

records.source: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἐκαθαρίσθη αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα.
records.gloss: And having stretched out the hand he touched him saying, I am willing, be cleansed; and immediately was cleansed of him the leprosy.
pieces: Jesus reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched him. "I do want to," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Be clean!" At once his leprosy was gone.

L.3: And stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

R.3: Jesus reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched the man. "I want to," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Be clean!" Right away the man's skin disease was gone, and he was clean.

decisions.choice: he touched him: touching an unclean person
decisions.reason: Touching a person with such a disease made one unclean (Leviticus 5:3). Instead of the uncleanness passing to Jesus, the man is made clean.

decisions.choice: his leprosy was cleansed: the disease was removed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the disease itself: it was taken away.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅρα μηδενὶ εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκον τὸ δῶρον ὃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And says to him the Jesus, See no one you tell, but go yourself show to the priest, and offer the gift that commanded Moses for a testimony to them.
pieces: Then Jesus said to him, "Be sure you do not tell anyone. Instead, go and let the priest examine you, and offer the gift Moses commanded, as evidence for them."

L.4: And Jesus says to him, "See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

R.4: Then Jesus told him, "Do not tell anyone about this. But go and let the priest look at you. Then give the offering that Moses commanded, so that people will know you are healed."

decisions.choice: show yourself to the priest: the law's steps for one who was healed (Leviticus 14)
decisions.reason: A priest had to examine the person and declare him clean, and offerings were then brought (Leviticus 14:1-32). Jesus sends the man to do what the law requires (5:17).

decisions.choice: a testimony to them: evidence to the priests and the people that he is clean
decisions.reason: "Them" is not named; it may be the priests or the people. The priest's declaration would also show what Jesus had done.

decisions.choice: tell no one: Jesus does not want to be known as a mere wonder-worker
alternatives: a test of the man's obedience
decisions.reason: Matthew records several such commands (9:30; 12:16). The reason is not stated here.

decisions.choice: says (L); said, told (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: Εἰσελθόντος δὲ αὐτοῦ εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἑκατόνταρχος παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ὁ παῖς μου βέβληται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ παραλυτικός, δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος.
records.gloss: Having entered then of him into Capernaum came to him a centurion imploring him \v 6 and saying, Lord, the servant of me is lying in the house paralyzed, terribly tormented.
pieces: When Jesus went into Capernaum, a centurion came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
"Lord," he said, "my servant is lying at home, paralyzed and in terrible pain."

L.5: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, appealing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
L.6: and saying, "Lord, my servant is lying at home paralyzed, terribly tormented."

R.5: When Jesus went into the town of Capernaum, a Roman army officer came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and begged for help.
R.6: He said, "Lord, my servant is at home in bed. He cannot move, and he is suffering terribly."

decisions.choice: a centurion: an army officer over about a hundred soldiers, a Gentile
decisions.reason: In Capernaum he probably served Herod Antipas, whose troops were organized on the Roman pattern. Jesus's words in 8:10-11 show he was not a Jew.

decisions.choice: servant: a household slave or servant, possibly a boy
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child, a son or a servant. Luke 7:2 calls him a slave, and the centurion speaks of his slave in 8:9.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address, and in Matthew more than that
decisions.reason: The word was a polite address to a superior. In Matthew those who come in faith call Jesus "Lord" (8:2, 6, 8, 25), and the reader hears the full sense.

decisions.choice: a Roman army officer
decisions.reason: Readable says what a centurion was. His troops followed the Roman pattern even if he served Herod.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced names Jesus.

records.heading: The centurion's faith

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἐγὼ ἐλθὼν θεραπεύσω αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And he says to him, I having come will heal him.
pieces: Jesus said to him, "I will come and heal him."

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "I will come and heal him."

R.7: Jesus said to him, "I will come and make him well."

decisions.choice: I will come and heal him: a promise
alternatives: a question: "Shall I come and heal him?"
decisions.reason: The Greek has no question mark of its own, and the emphatic "I" could be a surprised question from a Jew asked into a Gentile home. Most read it as a ready promise.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἑκατόνταρχος ἔφη· Κύριε, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς ἵνα μου ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην εἰσέλθῃς· ἀλλὰ μόνον εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήσεται ὁ παῖς μου·
records.gloss: And answering the centurion said, Lord, not I am worthy that of me under the roof you should come; but only say a word, and will be healed the servant of me;
pieces: The centurion replied, "Lord, I am not good enough for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to come into my house. Only give the command, and my servant will be well.

L.8: And the centurion answered and said, "Lord, I am not worthy that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} should come under my roof, but only say [the] word, and my servant will be healed.

R.8: The officer answered, "Lord, I am not good enough for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to come into my house. Just give the order, and my servant will get well.

decisions.choice: not worthy that you should come under my roof: a Gentile's home
decisions.reason: A Jew who entered a Gentile's house could be counted unclean (Acts 10:28). The centurion's humility also spares Jesus that.

decisions.choice: only say a word: give a command, from a distance
decisions.reason: He trusts that Jesus's spoken order is enough, as 8:9 explains.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address, and in Matthew more than that
decisions.reason: The word was a polite address to a superior. In Matthew those who come in faith call Jesus "Lord" (8:2, 6, 8, 25), and the reader hears the full sense.

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν, ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
records.gloss: Also for I a man am under authority, having under myself soldiers, and I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to the slave of me, Do this, and he does.
pieces: I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes, and another, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."

L.9: For I too am a man under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does [it]."

R.9: I am under the authority of officers above me, and I have soldiers under me. I tell one soldier, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."

decisions.choice: under authority: as his orders are obeyed, so Jesus's word will be obeyed
decisions.reason: Because he stands in a chain of command, his word carries his superiors' authority. He sees that Jesus's word carries God's authority over sickness.

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master
decisions.reason: The word names a slave, owned and bound to obey (6:24). The centurion's household obeys his word as soldiers do.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς ἀκολουθοῦσιν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, παρ’ οὐδενὶ τοσαύτην πίστιν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ εὗρον.
records.gloss: Having heard then the Jesus marveled and said to the following, Truly I say to you, with no one such faith in the Israel I found.
pieces: Jesus was amazed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard this. He said to those who were following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Truly I tell you, nowhere in Israel have I found faith as great as this.

L.10: And hearing [this], Jesus marveled and said to those following, "Truly I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.

R.10: When Jesus heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was amazed. He said to the people who were following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I tell you the truth, I have not found anyone in Israel who has faith as great as this man's.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus's authority and power
alternatives: belief in a set of teachings
decisions.reason: The centurion's faith is his confidence that Jesus's word will heal.

decisions.choice: Jesus marveled: he was truly amazed
decisions.reason: Matthew says plainly that Jesus was amazed, here at faith, and elsewhere he is amazed at unbelief (Mark 6:6).

decisions.choice: with no one in Israel, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: not even in Israel, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "not even in Israel have I found such faith", as in Luke 7:9. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν ἥξουσιν καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται μετὰ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν·
records.gloss: I say then to you that many from east and west will come and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens;
pieces: I tell you, many will come from the east and the west and will sit down to eat with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

L.11: And I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline [at table] with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,

R.11: I tell you, many people will come from all over the world, from east and west. They will sit and eat with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: many from east and west at the feast: Gentiles at God's banquet
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God gathering people from the ends of the earth to a feast (Isaiah 25:6-8; Psalm 107:3). After the centurion's faith, the many are most likely Gentiles, though the prophets' words first spoke of Israel's exiles.

decisions.choice: recline: eat at a feast, lying on couches around the table
decisions.reason: Guests at a banquet reclined. The kingdom is pictured as a great feast.

records.source: οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας ἐκβληθήσονται εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: the but sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the darkness the outer; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: But those who were born heirs of the kingdom will be thrown out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth."

L.12: but the {{gender:children|sons}} of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."

R.12: But the people who thought the kingdom belonged to them will be thrown outside into the dark. There they will cry and grind their teeth."

decisions.choice: sons of the kingdom: those who belonged to it by birth, the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "Sons of" names those to whom something belongs. Those who assumed a place by descent may lose it (3:9).

decisions.choice: the outer darkness, weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
alternatives: a literal place described in detail
decisions.reason: The darkness outside the lighted banquet hall pictures being shut out of the kingdom. Grinding the teeth shows anguish and rage. Matthew repeats the phrase (13:42, 50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The phrase covers men and women.

decisions.choice: those who were born heirs of the kingdom (B); the people who thought the kingdom belonged to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ· Ὕπαγε, ὡς ἐπίστευσας γενηθήτω σοι· καὶ ἰάθη ὁ παῖς ἐν τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.
records.gloss: And said the Jesus to the centurion, Go, as you believed let it be to you; and was healed the servant in the hour that.
pieces: Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go. It will happen for you just as you believed." And the servant was healed in that same hour.

L.13: And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; as you have believed, let it be done for you." And the servant was healed at that very hour.

R.13: Then Jesus said to the officer, "Go home. It will happen just as you believed it would." And at that very moment the servant was healed.

decisions.choice: as you have believed, let it be done: the healing answers his faith
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by his word; the centurion's trust is what Jesus answers.

decisions.choice: at that very hour: at the moment Jesus spoke
decisions.reason: The timing shows that the word alone healed, at a distance.

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Πέτρου εἶδεν τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτοῦ βεβλημένην καὶ πυρέσσουσαν·
records.gloss: And having come the Jesus into the house of Peter he saw the mother-in-law of him lying and fevering;
pieces: Jesus went into Peter's house and saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.

L.14: And when Jesus came into Peter's house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw his mother-in-law lying [sick] with a fever.

R.14: Jesus went to Peter's house. Peter's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever.

decisions.choice: Peter's house and mother-in-law: Peter was married and lived in Capernaum
decisions.reason: Paul mentions that Peter took his wife on his travels (1 Corinthians 9:5). Remains of a house in Capernaum have long been linked with Peter.

records.heading: Healing at Peter's house

records.source: καὶ ἥψατο τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ διηκόνει αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And he touched the hand of her, and left her the fever, and she arose and was serving him.
pieces: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began to wait on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.15: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.15: He touched her hand, and the fever went away. She got up and began to make a meal for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: serve: wait on, show hospitality, as a disciple serves
decisions.reason: The verb is used of serving at table and of ministering (4:11; 20:28). Her healing is complete: she is at once able to serve.

decisions.choice: him, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: them, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "them", as in Mark 1:31. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: make a meal for him
decisions.reason: Readable names the likely service.

records.source: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δαιμονιζομένους πολλούς· καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὰ πνεύματα λόγῳ, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ἐθεράπευσεν·
records.gloss: Evening then having come they brought to him demon-possessed many; and he cast out the spirits with a word, and all the badly having he healed;
pieces: That evening people brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} many who were controlled by demons. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed everyone who was sick.

L.16: And when evening had come, they brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} many who were demon-possessed, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick,

R.16: That evening people brought to Jesus many people who had demons in them. Jesus spoke, and the evil spirits left them. He healed all the people who were sick.

decisions.choice: the spirits with a word: evil spirits, driven out by his command
decisions.reason: Exorcists of the time used rituals and names. Jesus commands, and the spirits obey.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what kind of spirits.

records.source: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Αὐτὸς τὰς ἀσθενείας ἡμῶν ἔλαβεν καὶ τὰς νόσους ἐβάστασεν.
records.gloss: so that may be fulfilled the [thing] spoken through Isaiah the prophet saying, He the weaknesses of us took and the diseases bore.
pieces: This was so that the word spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled: "He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases."

L.17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "He {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} took our weaknesses and bore our diseases."

R.17: This made what the prophet Isaiah had said come true: "He took away our sicknesses and carried our diseases."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:4: the suffering servant who carries his people's griefs
decisions.reason: Isaiah's servant bears the sicknesses and pains of others and dies for their sins (Isaiah 53:4-12). Matthew applies the first line to Jesus's healings; the Hebrew words mean sicknesses and pains, and Matthew renders them that way rather than as the Greek Old Testament does ("sins").

decisions.choice: took, bore: took away and carried off
decisions.reason: He removes the diseases by taking them on himself, a hint of the cross to come.

decisions.choice: He himself, with a span on "himself"
decisions.reason: The emphatic pronoun refers to Jesus as the servant.

records.source: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πολλοὺς ὄχλους περὶ αὐτὸν ἐκέλευσεν ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
records.gloss: Having seen then the Jesus many crowds around him he ordered to depart to the other side.
pieces: When Jesus saw the crowds gathering around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to cross to the other side of the lake.

L.18: Now when Jesus saw great crowds around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to go over to the other side.

R.18: Jesus saw the big crowd around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to cross over to the other side of the lake.

decisions.choice: the other side: the east shore of the Sea of Galilee
alternatives: the far side of a river
decisions.reason: From Capernaum, the other side was the largely Gentile region of the Decapolis (8:28).

decisions.choice: of the lake (B, R); his followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is crossed; Readable says whom he told.

records.heading: The cost of following Jesus

records.source: καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς γραμματεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.
records.gloss: And having come one scribe said to him, Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.
pieces: A scribe came up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

L.19: And a scribe came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

R.19: A teacher of the law came to Jesus and said, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anywhere {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

decisions.choice: Teacher: a title of respect for a rabbi
decisions.reason: In Matthew outsiders and opponents call Jesus "Teacher" (12:38; 22:16), while disciples say "Lord" (8:21). The difference may hint that the scribe does not yet understand who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: a teacher of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.
records.gloss: And says to him the Jesus, The foxes holes have and the birds of the heaven nests, the but Son of the Man not has where the head he may lay.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Foxes have their holes and the birds in the sky their nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to rest {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head."

L.20: And Jesus says to him, "Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky [have] nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head."

R.20: Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes to live in, and birds have nests. But the Son of Man has no home where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can lie down to rest."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's way of speaking of himself
decisions.reason: This is the first time the title appears in Matthew. It is Jesus's own way of naming himself. In Hebrew and Aramaic "son of man" means a human being, and in Daniel 7:13-14 "one like a son of man" receives everlasting dominion from God. Jesus uses it of his lowliness (here), his suffering (17:22) and his coming in glory (24:30).

decisions.choice: nowhere to lay his head: following Jesus means sharing his homeless life
alternatives: Jesus was poor in every sense
decisions.reason: Jesus had a base in Capernaum (4:13), but his ministry kept him moving. The scribe must count the cost.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals as a title
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase as a title for himself, so it is capitalized.

records.source: ἕτερος δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι πρῶτον ἀπελθεῖν καὶ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.
records.gloss: Another then of the disciples said to him, Lord, allow me first to go and to bury the father of me.
pieces: Another of the disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, allow me first to go away and bury my father."

L.21: And another of the disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father."

R.21: Another of Jesus's followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."

decisions.choice: bury my father: the most sacred duty a son owed his parents
decisions.reason: Burying one's parents was a duty that came before many religious obligations (Tobit 4:3). The father may have just died, or the son may mean staying until he dies.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι, καὶ ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς.
records.gloss: The but Jesus says to him, Follow me, and leave the dead to bury the of themselves dead.
pieces: But Jesus told him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Leave the dead to bury their own dead."

L.22: But Jesus says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and let the dead bury their own dead."

R.22: But Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now. Let those who are dead to God bury their own dead."

decisions.choice: let the dead bury their own dead: let those without the life of the kingdom see to it
decisions.reason: The saying is shocking on purpose. The first "dead" are most likely the spiritually dead, those who do not follow Jesus. Nothing comes before the call to follow him (10:37).

decisions.choice: those who are dead to God
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the first "dead", which the meaning note marks as uncertain.

records.source: Καὶ ἐμβάντι αὐτῷ εἰς πλοῖον ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having entered he into a boat followed him the disciples of him.
pieces: Then Jesus stepped into the boat, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.23: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.23: Then Jesus got into a boat, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: followed him: the word for discipleship, after 8:19-22
decisions.reason: Matthew has just told of two would-be followers. Now the disciples follow Jesus into the boat and into the storm.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced names Jesus.

records.heading: Jesus calms the storm

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ὥστε τὸ πλοῖον καλύπτεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκάθευδεν.
records.gloss: And behold, a shaking great arose in the sea, so that the boat to be covered by the waves, he but was sleeping.
pieces: Without warning a great storm broke over the lake, and waves were sweeping over the boat. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asleep.

L.24: And look, a great shaking arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was sleeping.

R.24: Suddenly a very strong storm came on the lake. The waves were so big that water was coming into the boat. But Jesus was sleeping.

decisions.choice: a great shaking: a violent storm
decisions.reason: The word usually means an earthquake; here it is a storm that shook the sea. Matthew uses the same word for the shakings of the last days and of Jesus's death and rising (24:7; 27:54; 28:2).

decisions.choice: he was sleeping: rest that shows complete trust
alternatives: he did not know of the danger
decisions.reason: Sleeping in danger is a sign of trust in God (Psalm 3:6; 4:9).

decisions.choice: look (L); without warning (B); suddenly (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ προσελθόντες ἤγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, σῶσον, ἀπολλύμεθα.
records.gloss: And having come they woke him saying, Lord, save, we are perishing.
pieces: They came and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Lord, save us!" they cried. "We are about to die!"

L.25: And they came and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, save [us]; we are perishing!"

R.25: The followers went to Jesus and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up. They said, "Lord, save us! We are going to die!"

decisions.choice: Lord, save: a cry for rescue, in the words of prayer
decisions.reason: The words echo the Psalms' cries to God (Psalm 69:2; 107:28).

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
records.gloss: And he says to them, Why fearful are you, little-faiths?
pieces: He said to them, "Why are you so frightened, you who have so little faith?"

L.26: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?"

R.26: Jesus said to them, "Why are you so afraid? Your faith is so small!"

decisions.choice: little faith: trust that gives way under pressure
decisions.reason: As in 6:30, the word rebukes disciples whose faith is real but weak.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: τότε ἐγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τοῖς ἀνέμοις καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.
records.gloss: Then having arisen he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a calm great.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and spoke sharply to the winds and the waves, and everything became completely calm.

L.26: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.

R.26: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and gave a command to the wind and the waves. The wind stopped, and the lake became very calm.

decisions.choice: he rebuked the winds and the sea: what God does in the Psalms
decisions.reason: God rebukes the sea and stills the storm (Psalm 106:9; 107:29). Jesus does what Scripture says God does.

decisions.choice: spoke sharply to (B); gave a command to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the rebuke for a reader who may not expect it of weather.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Ποταπός ἐστιν οὗτος ὅτι καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ ἡ θάλασσα αὐτῷ ὑπακούουσιν;
records.gloss: The but men marveled saying, What sort is this one that even the winds and the sea him obey?
pieces: They were amazed. "What kind of person is this?" they said. "Even the winds and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

L.27: And the men marveled, saying, "What sort [of person] is this, that even the winds and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"

R.27: The followers were amazed. They said, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the waves obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: the men: the people in the boat, the disciples
alternatives: other people who heard the story
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, which may set them against the one whom wind and sea obey.

decisions.choice: what sort of person is this: the question points to God
decisions.reason: In Scripture only God commands the sea (Psalm 89:10; Job 38:8-11). Matthew leaves the question for the reader to answer.

decisions.choice: they (B); the followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the group without the generic "men".

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πέραν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γαδαρηνῶν ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ δύο δαιμονιζόμενοι ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἐξερχόμενοι, χαλεποὶ λίαν ὥστε μὴ ἰσχύειν τινὰ παρελθεῖν διὰ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἐκείνης.
records.gloss: And having come of him to the other side into the region of the Gadarenes met him two demon-possessed out of the tombs coming, violent very, so that not was able anyone to pass through the way that.
pieces: When Jesus arrived on the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes, two men controlled by demons came out of the tombs to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were so dangerous that nobody dared to use that road.

L.28: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed [men] met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, coming out of the tombs, extremely violent, so that no one was able to pass by that way.

R.28: Jesus arrived on the other side of the lake, in the land of the Gadarenes. Two men who had demons in them came out of the burial caves and met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were so dangerous that no one could walk on that road.

decisions.choice: Gadarenes, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ over the name, as they do in Mark 5:1 and Luke 8:26. Gadara was a town about six miles southeast of the lake. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two men
alternatives: one man, as in Mark and Luke
decisions.reason: Mark 5:2 and Luke 8:27 tell of one man. Matthew has two here, as he has two blind men in 20:30; he does not explain.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial caves, unclean places outside the town
decisions.reason: Tombs were cut into the rock. Living among the dead made a person unclean and cut off.

decisions.choice: burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable describes them.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced names Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ;
records.gloss: And behold, they cried out saying, What to us and to you, Son of the God?
pieces: They screamed, "Son of God, what business do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have with us?

L.29: And look, they cried out, saying, "What [is there] to us and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Son of God?

R.29: They shouted, "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want with us, Son of God?

decisions.choice: what to us and to you: what do we have in common? Leave us alone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom rejects someone's interference (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: Son of God: the demons know who Jesus is
decisions.reason: God called Jesus his Son at the baptism (3:17); the tempter knew it (4:3); now the demons cry it out, while the disciples are still asking (8:27).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: ἦλθες ὧδε πρὸ καιροῦ βασανίσαι ἡμᾶς;
records.gloss: Did you come here before time to torment us?
pieces: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here to torment us before the appointed time?"

L.29: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here before the time to torment us?"

R.29: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here to punish us before the time God has set?"

decisions.choice: before the time: before the appointed day of judgment
decisions.reason: The demons know their end is set for the final judgment (25:41). They see that end breaking in early with Jesus.

decisions.choice: the time God has set
decisions.reason: Readable says whose time it is.

records.source: ἦν δὲ μακρὰν ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀγέλη χοίρων πολλῶν βοσκομένη.
records.gloss: There was then far from them a herd of pigs many feeding.
pieces: Some distance away a large herd of pigs was feeding.

L.30: Now far from them a herd of many pigs was feeding.

R.30: Some distance away, a big herd of pigs was eating.

decisions.choice: a herd of pigs: in a Gentile region
decisions.reason: The law forbade Jews to eat pork (Leviticus 11:7). A large herd fits the Gentile towns of the Decapolis.

records.source: οἱ δὲ δαίμονες παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἐκβάλλεις ἡμᾶς, ἀπόστειλον ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀγέλην τῶν χοίρων.
records.gloss: The then demons were begging him saying, If you cast out us, send us into the herd of the pigs.
pieces: The demons kept begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."

L.31: And the demons begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs."

R.31: The demons begged Jesus, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us leave these men, send us into that herd of pigs."

decisions.choice: begged: kept begging
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures repeated pleading. The demons know they must obey.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε.
records.gloss: And he said to them, Go.
pieces: "Go!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them.

decisions.choice: Go: one word is enough
decisions.reason: As with the sick (8:8, 16), Jesus's single word is obeyed.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἀπῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους· καὶ ἰδοὺ ὥρμησεν πᾶσα ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ ἀπέθανον ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν.
records.gloss: They then having come out went into the pigs; and behold, rushed all the herd down the steep bank into the sea, and they died in the waters.
pieces: The demons came out and entered the pigs, and at once the whole herd stampeded down the slope into the lake and drowned.

L.32: And they came out and went into the pigs; and look, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they died in the waters.

R.32: The demons left the men and went into the pigs. Then the whole herd ran down the steep hill into the lake and drowned.

decisions.choice: the herd rushed into the sea: the demons' power to destroy, and its end
decisions.reason: The sea was a picture of chaos and death. The destruction shows what the demons would have done to the men.

decisions.choice: look (L); at once (B); then (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: οἱ δὲ βόσκοντες ἔφυγον, καὶ ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν πάντα καὶ τὰ τῶν δαιμονιζομένων.
records.gloss: The then feeding fled, and having gone into the city they reported all things and the [things] of the demon-possessed.
pieces: The men looking after the pigs ran off into the town and reported everything, including what had happened to the men with demons.

L.33: And those tending [them] fled, and going into the town they reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed [men].

R.33: The men who were taking care of the pigs ran away to the town. They told everyone what had happened, and what had happened to the men who had demons.

decisions.choice: the town: probably Gadara or a village near the lake
decisions.reason: The word can mean a town of any size.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ πᾶσα ἡ πόλις ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ὑπάντησιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν παρεκάλεσαν ὅπως μεταβῇ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And behold, all the city went out to meet the Jesus, and having seen him they begged that he would depart from the region of them.
pieces: At that the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to go away from their district.

L.34: And look, the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to leave their region.

R.34: So all the people of the town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to go away from their land.

decisions.choice: they begged him to leave: fear and loss outweigh wonder
decisions.reason: The demons begged to go into the pigs; the town begs Jesus to go away. Matthew does not say why, but the loss of the herd and fear of his power fit the story.

decisions.choice: look (L); at that (B); so (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.
